column15: Verified via producer's own domain (oldballantruan.com, Angus Dundee's dedicated site for this brand): "heavily peated malted barley", "Speyside Peated Single Malt" -- corroborates heavy peat directly from the producer's domain (satisfies the positive-peat rule). Owner Angus Dundee Distillers confirmed via tomintoulwhisky.com footer. Upgraded from low to high confidence.

Producer identified via alcomag.ua spec sheet: Виробник (Producer) = BARDINET S.A., Країна (Country) = Іспанія (Spain), barcode 8410490268859 (EAN prefix 841 = Spain, consistent). Bardinet is the same French/Spanish spirits company already known in this KB for Sir Edwards. The label itself states Type = Бурбон (Bourbon) despite the Spanish origin -- almost certainly not genuine Kentucky bourbon, so defaultTypeName is left empty rather than asserting an implausible category; flagged for human review. Not the same producer as the differently-spelled "Jim Bardett" row.

Corrected countryCode from GB-SCT to EE (Estonia) -- verified via the producer's own site, koch1872.com ("Koch OÜ, Lootsi 10, 10151 Tallinn"), which lists Old Barny Whisky (40% vol) with three Estonian-registered EANs (4742883... prefix). Not a Scotch whisky at all; region/legalRegion cleared accordingly. defaultTypeName=blend inferred from category convention for a basic no-frills product (not explicitly stated on the producer page).

Verified as genuine Scotch Whisky branding (label reads "Single Malt Scotch Whisky") via an opened Silpo listing; Whiskybase also lists separate "Old Castle Blended Scotch Whisky" and "Old Castle Finest Scotch Whisky" entries under the same brand, so this is a multi-type range -- defaultTypeName left empty. No specific bottler/owner company confirmed this session (a possible link to Ukraine's Global Spirits/Khortytsa could not be confirmed) -- flagged for review. Note: oldcastle.ck.ua is an unrelated Cherkasy restaurant, not the producer -- do not use as a source.

Verified via an opened Whisky.Auction lot: "Old Glasgow Blended Scotch Whisky", bottled 1983, Bottler = Hart Brothers, Country = Scotland -- bottlerSlug set to the already-live hart-brothers. Other retail listings (Total Wine, geo-blocked this session) also describe an "Old Glasgow 8 Year Old Single Malt" (Speyside) under the same name, possibly a separate modern product -- unconfirmed this session, flagged for a human to check whether a second row is warranted. No peat/smoke mentioned in any source.

Re-verified via Wikipedia: rye whiskey, manufacturer Suntory Global Spirits, produced at the Jim Beam distillery (Clermont, Kentucky) -- confirms the seed's fields exactly (owner, parent=jim-beam, type=rye). America's oldest continuously produced whiskey brand (est. 1810).

Re-verified via the producer's own site (buffalotracedistillery.com): Kentucky Straight Bourbon Whiskey, wheated mash, bottled by Buffalo Trace under the Van Winkle brand. Tasting notes mention a "smoky wheat finish" -- standard bourbon oak-char language, not peat; confirms peatProfile=none.

Re-verified via the producer's own site: 8-year cask-strength single-barrel Kentucky straight bourbon. No smoke/peat in tasting notes (oak, vanilla, brown sugar, baking spices only). Sourced-distillery rumor (Heaven Hill) remains unconfirmed, so no parentSlug given, matching the seed's caution.

Fully verified via the producer's own domain (bravenewspirits.com/volume-brands): "Old Smitty's -- Single Malt Scotch Whisky ... selected from one of Scotland's finest distilleries" -- no peat/smoke language, unlike their separate "Lighthouse" peated/unpeated blend, so peatProfile=none. Brave New Spirits Ltd is an independent whisky bottling company based in Glasgow (confirmed via whisky.auction: Country=Scotland, Classification=Single Malt Scotch Whisky, "bottled for Brave New Spirits"). One IWSC competition entry's tasting note mentions "bonfire smoke" while a different IWSC entry for the same product does not -- kept peatProfile=none per the producer's own consistent messaging, but flagging the conflicting third-party note for a human reviewer.

Re-verified via an opened OKWine retailer page, which independently repeats the full Tullymet distillery history (built 1812 as Auchnagie, renamed Tullymet 1890, closed 1911) and states Country=Scotland -- confirms the seed's research exactly. The producer's own site (oldtullymet.com) could not be reached this session (connection denied/failed).

Corrected from fully unresearched to verified: "Old Woody 8 Year Old Kentucky Bourbon", 40%, 70cl -- a genuine Kentucky straight bourbon (not an unclassifiable own-label). No owning company identified this session; likely an undisclosed-source NDP bottling. No peat (standard bourbon).

Corrected countryCode from XX to IE: verified via an opened Bulgarian retailer page stating "Произход: Ирландия" / "Дестилирано, отлежало и бутилирано в Ирландия" (distilled, matured and bottled in Ireland) for O'Patrick Irish Whiskey, triple-distilled, 40% ABV. The EAN barcode prefix (301, on the Whisky Auctioneer listing) suggests French registration for the brand/importer, but "Irish Whiskey" is a protected designation requiring Irish distillation regardless of who owns/bottles the brand. No owning company confirmed. No peat (standard Irish blend).

Re-verified via an opened retailer/collection page: "Rhetoric" is a Kentucky Straight Bourbon release under the Orphan Barrel collection with several age statements (20/21/24/25 years). Matches the seed's fields; still no confirmed specific source distillery for this release, so kind stays blend.

Corrected from unclassified to verified: PennyPacker is a Kentucky Straight Bourbon distilled by Heaven Hill (confirmed via an opened Bourbon & Banter review: "DISTILLER: Heaven Hill then shipped to Borco for bottling and return to U.S. shelves"), 3+ years, undisclosed mashbill (>=70% corn). Also sold in Ukraine (goodwine.ua, silpo.ua per search results). No peat.

Corrected from unverified to verified via an opened packaging-design portfolio page describing the real product: a high-corn-mashbill bourbon blended from barrels aged 5-6 years in virgin oak casks, "deep in bourbon country" (US branding). No owning company named. No peat.

Upgraded to high confidence: verified directly on the producer's own domain (ianmacleod.com/brands/pigs-nose) -- blended from Lowland/Speyside/Highland malt and grain whiskies, tasting notes "gentle and sweet ... slightly coastal", no peat/smoke claimed. Confirms the seed's acquisition history (ex-Spencerfield Spirit Company, bought by Ian Macleod 2016) via Wikipedia. One IWSC competition entry for this whisky separately notes "bonfire smoke" while another IWSC entry for the same product does not -- kept peatProfile=none per the producer's own domain (the rule's evidentiary bar) but flagging the conflict for a human reviewer. bottlerSlug set to new row ian-macleod (see below).

Major correction: this IS a genuine whisky, verified directly on the producer's own domain (poligrappa.com, Jacopo Poli's distillery, Veneto/Bassano del Grappa, Italy): "Segretario di Stato ... Raw material: Pure Malt, pleasantly peaty; aged 5 years and finished in Amarone barrels." "Pleasantly peaty" ("gradevolmente torbato") read as light rather than heavy -- the positive peat claim satisfies the corroboration rule via the producer's own domain. Not a mislabeled grappa product as the seed suspected (the seed's poligrappa.com fetch apparently failed/404'd; it loads fine this session). kind upgraded to distillery since Poli genuinely distills it themselves ("artisanal distillation with a discontinuous bain-marie still").

Major correction: fully identified via two opened sources. Full name "Prohibited Ley Seca" (De La Enmienda XVIII) is a genuine Mexican Single Malt whisky produced for Cervecera Mexicana S.A. de C.V. (also known for Day of the Dead and Mexicali beers), distilled from 100% malted barley from Mexico's Bajío region, aged 3 years in lightly-toasted ex-bourbon barrels, 40% ABV. Not a Prohibition-themed cocktail as the seed suspected -- a real, current product. Tasting notes mention "a bit of smoke" on the finish but read as dark-roast-coffee/char character rather than a peat claim, and no source states peat explicitly -- kept unknown per the caution rule.

Re-verified via an opened Breaking Bourbon review: "Company: Heaven Hill, Distillery: Heaven Hill" -- "Quality House Distillers" is one of the DBA names Heaven Hill trades under. Confirms the seed exactly. The range spans both a Straight Bourbon and a separate "Mild & Mellow Kentucky Blended Whiskey" under the same Quality House name (confirmed via retailer images), so defaultTypeName correctly stays empty. "Touch of smokiness" in the nose is standard bourbon oak-char language, not peat.

Corrected from unresearched to fully verified via the producer's own domain: "Ragtime Rye -- American Straight Whiskey. Distilled from rye proudly grown in New York State" by New York Distilling Company (Brooklyn, NY craft distillery). No peat (standard American rye).

Re-verified via an opened German retailer page, which categorizes it under Whisky > Whiskies worldwide > Irish whiskey. Part of a wider Rammstein-branded spirits range (rum, gin, vodka, tequila, wine) tied to the German rock band. Matches the seed's fields exactly. No peat.

Corrected from fully unresolved to verified: Reki is a genuine Okinawan blended whisky by Helios Shuzo (Helios Distillery) -- confirmed on the producer's own domain (whisky.helios-shop.jp). Blends in-house malt whisky with selected Scottish malt whisky and grain whisky, aged three years in Okinawa's tropical climate. Detailed tasting notes (yeast, rice husk, vanilla, spice, mango, pineapple, coffee) carry no smoke/peat descriptor across two independent reviews.

Re-verified via the producer's own site: Richmond, Virginia craft distillery (est. 2008) producing bourbon, rye and other grain whiskies (confirmed a distinct "Reservoir Rye" product line). No peat mentioned; defaultTypeName stays empty (multi-type range).

new row for pigs-nose. Independent, family-owned Scotch whisky company (est. 1933, Broxburn, Scotland); owns Glengoyne, Tamdhu and Rosebank distilleries plus Edinburgh Gin, and blends/brands Pig's Nose, Smokehead (peated Islay-style), King Robert II, Isle of Skye, Hedges & Butler among others -- no single house peat style, so peatProfile is left unknown at this umbrella level (peat belongs on each individual brand/distillery row).
